task: Implement a stateful TCP byte-stream frame codec with 4-byte big-endian length prefix and arbitrary chunk reassembly

blueprint.task_description: Implement a stateful TCP byte-stream frame codec with 4-byte big-endian length prefix and arbitrary chunk reassembly
blueprint.first_principles_invariant: Byte-Stream Continuity Invariant: Transport chunk boundaries are completely arbitrary and independent of logical message boundaries. A decoder MUST append incoming bytes to a persistent unread buffer and loop to extract 0, 1, or N complete frames only when their full payload is present, leaving partial trailing bytes in the buffer for future calls.
naive_intuition_traps: Assuming 1 `feed_chunk()` call equals 1 logical frame (failing when a frame is split 1 byte at a time or when 3 frames arrive in 1 chunk).
Consuming or discarding buffer bytes before verifying the full frame length is available in the buffer.
Replacing escaped sequences in-place with naive `.replace()` where double-escapes (`\\`) get corrupted.
minimal_counter_examples: Feed a 20-byte encoded frame 1 byte at a time (`for b in frame: feed(bytes([b]))`) -> first 19 calls return `[]`, 20th call returns `[payload]`.
Feed 3 concatenated frames in a single `feed_chunk(f1 + f2 + f3)` call -> must return all 3 decoded payloads in one list.
Payload containing literal delimiter/escape bytes -> must round-trip identically (`decode(encode(raw)) == raw`).
boundary_checklist: Empty / zero-element input handled without crash
Single-element and tie-breaking / wrap-around boundary tested
All 3 Feynman minimal counter-examples encoded as unit tests
AST Quality Gate (`evlop audit --min-score 100`) passes with 0 findings
blueprint.universal_mental_model: Stateful Accumulator Buffer with Atomic Frame-Boundary Commit
